text:
anya: heads up — saw a spike of pod evictions in the us-west-2-gpu pool starting ~10:03am. multiple nodes briefly NotReady, then kubelet triggered evictions. anyone else seeing net-probe flapping?

santiago: seeing it. `kubectl get nodes` showed a bunch of `NotReady` for ~30-90s then back. pods with local ephemeral state got evicted.

mike: pulled kubelet logs on a node, snippet:
```
May 12 10:04:12 ip-10-0-6-14 kubelet[1234]: NetworkPlugin cni failed on the status hook: cni returned error: failed to set up pod net: write udp 10.0.6.14:34567->10.0.6.1:6789: write: message too long
May 12 10:04:13 ip-10-0-6-14 kubelet[1234]: Node not ready: NodeNetworkUnavailable: net health check failed
```

julia: on the same host `ip link` shows one ENA interface with MTU 9000 and the bonded/bridge with 1500. suspect fragmentation on the node-to-node probes (we use 9000 on host net for RDMA but CNI overlay is 1500).

anya: that would explain probe failures — probes use UDP/ICMP small packets, but if fragmentation or DF flags cause drop then k8s sees transient network death. this looks like false positives: underlying kernel + cni mismatch. :thinking_face:

santiago: yep. I also saw repeated RX errors in dmesg on the NIC around the same window. ran `ethtool -S eth0 | grep tx_err` — not huge but correlated.

oncall-bot: :rotating_light: alert: eviction-spike detected (evictions/sec > baseline) 10:03:00-10:09:30 — affected pool: us-west-2-gpu — runbook linked -> /runbooks/node-eviction.md

mike: short-term mitigation ideas: 1) bump controller-manager `--pod-eviction-timeout` to 10m and `--node-monitor-grace-period` to 2m to avoid 1m flaps causing evictions, 2) schedule a CNI/MTU rollout to align host and pod MTU, 3) cordon + drain the few noisy nodes and repro.

julia: prefer not to change timeouts cluster-wide without SLAs signoff. we can instead taint the noisy nodes and migrate stateful pods, or set a temporary higher toleration for eviction-causing taint.

anya: plan: santiago will run a fast diag script across affected nodes (dmesg|grep -i "eth.*error"; ethtool -k; ip link show; cat /etc/cni/net.d/*) and collect CNI MTU, kernel offload settings. if it's MTU mismatch we push CNI config to 9000 or teach the overlay to handle fragmentation.

santiago: running diag now on nodes: ip-10-0-6-{12,14,19}. uploading logs to /tmp/net-flap-1748005432.tar.gz and attaching to incident ticket.

mike: while diag runs, i'll patch oncall dashboard to show NodeNetworkUnavailable rate and add a temporary alert suppression for the eviction-alert to avoid noisy pages while we remediate.

julia: reminder — if this is RDMA/GPUDirect related, changing MTU has perf implications. let's test on one node first. also add an audit note so we can revert.

anya: agreed. owner: santiago to run MTU test + small pod-to-pod iperf and icmp checks. mike to mute noisy alert and prepare rollback steps. i'll draft a short postmortem template and include recommended kube-controller-manager flags to consider after root cause confirmed.

santiago: update in 25m with findings. early hypothesis: CNI bridge at 1500 vs host RDMA at 9000 causing ICMP/UDP fragmentation + kernel drop, leading kubelet health probes to mark NetUnavailable briefly -> controller triggers pod eviction path.

julia: long-term action items: 1) add a runbook section for MTU mismatches and RDMA nodes, 2) add a rolling CNI MTU validator into node-autorepair job, 3) review eviction timeout defaults for GPU pools.

anya: thanks all — keeping this thread as the single source. :thumbsup:

oncall-bot: incident ticket created #INC-2026-1748005432 (assigned to santiago).
